raw_segments.text: May we not say that the necessary bodily pleasures are good in the sense, in which that which
is not bad is good, or that they are good only up to a certain point, because such states
or movements as cannot have too much of the better, cannot have too much of pleasure,
but those which can of the former can also of the latter.
Now the bodily pleasures do admit of excess.
In fact the low bad man is such because he pursues the excess of them instead of those
which are necessary, meat, drink, and the objects of other animal appetites do give
pleasure to all, but not in right manner or degree to all.
But his relation to pain is exactly the contrary.
It is not excessive pain, but pain at all, that he avoids which makes him to be in this
way too a bad low man, because only in the case of him who pursues excessive pleasure
is pain contrary to excessive pleasure.
